concurrent development is inherently less efficient than serial development, regardless of team size or programming practices.

The main takeaway from our work is that
the productivity of two-person teams is highly variable and depends on the type of work they are performing.
the productivity of two programmers working together is not necessarily higher than that of two programmers working independently.
the productivity of two-person teams, whether they are working concurrently or independently, is significantly lower than the productivity of teams of all other sizes.
